Bug_Details:
Category: Perf regression. Reported as "Allocates Memory" by annotation-reachability.

A method annotated with @NoAllocation transitively calls new.

Example:

class C implements I {  @NoAllocation  void directlyAllocatingMethod() {    new Object();  }}
Bug_Explanation: The @NoAllocation annotation is used to indicate that a method should not allocate memory. However, the directlyAllocatingMethod method violates this contract by creating a new Object instance, which allocates memory, thereby triggering the CHECKERS_ALLOCATES_MEMORY bug.
Trigger_Explanation: The testShowBug test case calls the showBug method of the MemoryAllocationExample class. The showBug method internally calls directlyAllocatingMethod, which has the @NoAllocation annotation but allocates memory by creating a new Object. This violates the @NoAllocation contract, thereby triggering the CHECKERS_ALLOCATES_MEMORY bug and causing the test to fail.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that the test passed without any errors or failures, suggesting that the bug was not triggered during the test execution.
